body: The startStructuredOutputCapture function in go/internal/harnessx/schema.go does not remove the .agentfield-out-* directory in its cleanup return function (line 302-311). The SDK harness contract requires the SDK to create .agentfield-out-* under opts.ProjectDir containing .agentfield_output.json and remove it before returning. However, this repo's .gitignore does NOT list .agentfield-out-*, and the function's return cleanup only cancels the context and returns captured bytes — it does NOT remove the directory. If the SDK fails to delete the directory (e.g., process crash), surviving .agentfield-out-* dirs remain. Since .agentfield-out-* is untracked-and-not-ignored, these surviving dirs fall into reviewerUntrackedPaths/verifierUntrackedPaths and will be os.Rename'd away by archiveNewReviewerScratch/archiveNewVerifierScratch before anyone can inspect the output. Evidence: (1) schema.go:302-311 return func() { cancel(); <-done; mu.Lock(); defer mu.Unlock(); if ambiguous || len(latest) == 0 { return }; return append([]byte(nil), latest...) } — no os.RemoveAll or directory cleanup. (2) SDK harness contract: 'it must create its structured-output directory under opts.ProjectDir ... named .agentfield-out-* ... and remove it before returning'. (3) This repo's .gitignore does not list .agentfield-out-*. (4) Surviving dirs .agentfield-out-3193973803 exist in the repo, confirming the leak.
suggestion: Add directory cleanup in the startStructuredOutputCapture return function: os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(projectDir, '.agentfield-out-*')) or track .agentfield-out-* in .gitignore and ensure removal on all exit paths, or have the return function remove the captured directory before returning.
title: Structured output capture leaves surviving .agentfield-out-* directories risking data loss
